get_block_wrapper_attributes (class-wp-block-supports.php) is only visible in wp-includes/blocks/*.php through Populator::populateFileStorage's transitive referenced_classlikes leak (@param WP_Block -> class-wp-block.php references WP_Block_Supports), which depends on file population order (snippet temp/vd-wp-undefined-c: reported or not by both versions depending on dir order); population code unchanged, so likely a scan-order difference, not a deliberate change.

6.x switched off all function checks for the rest of the scope after any function_exists() (wp-load.php:24 `function_exists('error_reporting')`, reached from every admin/top-level script via require __DIR__.'/wp-load.php'; theme/includes files have their own function_exists guards before the reported lines); 8e1b0d0158 (PR #12657, #10179) makes a literal function_exists() guard only that function, so the WP functions Psalm cannot reach through the unresolvable ABSPATH . WPINC includes are now reported like the 42k 6.x already reports (snippet temp/vd-wp-undefined-b).

Calls on the right of `is_callable($cb) && f()` (widgets.php `is_callable(...) && (... || did_action())`, dashboard.php `is_callable(...) && current_user_can()`): 8e1b0d0158 (PR #12657) makes the right operand of && and the if body keep the left operand's function-check state, and is_callable() still switches function checks off; the functions exist in WP (only unreachable through unresolvable includes).

6.x switched off all constant checks after a negated defined() (`if (!defined('ABSPATH'))`, `!defined('WP_ADMIN')` in wp-load.php, wp-admin/admin.php, blocks/index.php...); 2593074387 (#5292) keeps them on, so constants defined only behind unresolvable includes (WPINC, ABSPATH, WP_PLUGIN_DIR...) are now reported like the ones 6.x already reported elsewhere.

Constants that are defined: guarded by `if (!defined('ABSPATH')) die` (menu-header.php) now known after the guard (2593074387/5c22eeeb17, #5292), or defined unconditionally in the analysed file itself (class-ftp.php:75 define('FTP_OS_Unix'), used in methods when the file is analysed through an include) now found by d02b960399 (constants of the code's file looked up after the root file's).

entries.note: `/** @param object|resource $h */ curl_getinfo($h)`: 6.x ArgumentTypeCoercion, 7.x InvalidArgument; the object part can be a CurlHandle, so at most PossiblyInvalidArgument. `object` alone or `object|null` still give ArgumentTypeCoercion in 7.x: only the resource member flips it. Commit not found. Snippet confirmed.

entries.message: Cannot call function on non-empty-mixed
entries.note: `$prev = set_error_handler(function () use (&$prev) { return $prev ? $prev(...) : false; })`: 6.x reported UndefinedVariable $prev and stopped; 7.x resolves the by-reference use (mixed inside the closure) and calls it. Snippet confirmed.

Closure handler `function ($type, $msg, $file, $line) use (&$prev)`: 6.x gave MixedArgument (by-ref use undefined), 7.x checks the closure and flags it because the callmap marks $errfile/$errline optional though PHP always passes them. Same strictness already hits closures without by-ref uses in 6.x (InvalidArgument); newly surfaced by the by-ref fix. Snippet confirmed.

set_error_handler callmap signature has $errfile/$errline optional, so a handler closure requiring 4 params is rejected though PHP always passes them; pre-existing in 6.x, newly reached here once the by-ref `use (&$prev)` resolves. Snippet confirmed.
6.x inferred SplObjectStorage<never, ...> for an empty-initialised storage property and rejected every key; 7.x keeps the declared template.

Psalm 7 auto-enables psalm/plugin-phpunit and plugin-mockery because laravel/framework composer.json require-dev lists phpunit/phpunit and mockery/mockery (51c7ec62b7, Config::FIRST_PARTY_PLUGINS, reads require-dev); the corpus installs --no-dev so the real libraries are absent and only the plugins' partial stubs exist: plugin-phpunit's TestCase.phpstub declares an empty `abstract class Assert`, so PHPUnit::assertTrue() etc. become UndefinedMethod (6.x: UndefinedClass). Newly reachable after the Conditionable docblock parses (template params of when/unless).

InvocationMockerImplementation (class-level @no-named-arguments, honoured since b34d358514) implements InvocationMocker::with*(mixed ...$arguments), whose interface methods accept named arguments; for a variadic the names do matter.

b34d358514 applies class-level @no-named-arguments to every method, and FunctionLikeAnalyzer then flags parameterless overrides (Countable::count, Iterator::*, IteratorAggregate::getIterator, FilterIterator::accept, RecursiveIterator::*, Stringable::__toString, InvocationStubber::seal) where named arguments cannot occur. Snippet: /** @no-named-arguments */ final class C implements Countable { public function count(): int { return 0; } } -> 7.17.0 MethodSignatureMismatch, 6.21.3 none.
PHPUnit classes carry class-level @no-named-arguments (Generator.php:58, Job.php:17, Assert), honoured since b34d358514; these calls pass named or string-keyed arguments to them.
Variadics of methods of @no-named-arguments classes are now lists (class-level tag honoured, b34d358514), e.g. FileCollection::__construct(File ...$files) assigned to list<File>.
Variadics under class-level @no-named-arguments are now lists (b34d358514), e.g. InvocationMockerImplementation.php:47 $arguments.
DOMElement::$ownerDocument is ?DOMDocument (an element built with new DOMElement has none), so assert($ownerDocument !== null) in Xml/Migration/Migrations/* is meaningful.

entries.message: Cannot call an impure constructor from a pure context
entries.note: `new DateTimeImmutable($parts[0])` in a @pure method: the ctor reads the clock and the default timezone, but 7.x treats it as pure because the stub ctor in CoreImmutableClasses.phpstub has an empty body and applyTrivialConstructorCapabilities() (efbe0447c5) gives it NONE (no stub check). Snippet `/** @pure */ function f(): DateTimeImmutable { return new DateTimeImmutable(); }`: 6.x ImpureMethodCall, 7.x silent (new DateTime() still reported).

entries.message: Cannot call an impure constructor from a pure context
entries.note: Constructors of readonly/immutable classes that only assign promoted params (ControlSequenceIntroducer, OperatingSystemCommand, DirectedGraph, Edge, TreeNode, LeafNode...) are trivial write-this-props constructors in 7.x (efbe0447c5), so `new` in a @pure function is fine (snippet confirmed).
Graph\bfs/dfs/has_path/shortest_path call enqueue/push/pop on a Queue/Stack/PriorityQueue created locally: a pure context may mutate fresh objects in the capabilities model (bb1042b9fd).

entries.message: Cannot call an impure function from a mutation-free context
entries.note: DirectedGraph/UndirectedGraph call a local recursive closure $dfsCheck that only writes captured fresh state (closure_state rule, bb1042b9fd).
Assigning a recursive closure to a by-ref captured local ($dfsCheck, $build) only touches local state; no longer flagged by the capabilities model (bb1042b9fd).

entries.message: The context is read-props but method Locale::getDefault requires impure
entries.note: Locale::getDefault() reads the intl.default_locale global; Locale::default() is annotated mutation-free. 6.x did not check static builtin calls from mutation-free contexts.

Effectively pure intl/date builtins (Locale::getPrimaryLanguage/getScript/getRegion/getDisplay* with an explicit locale, IntlTimeZone::createTimeZone/getIanaID/getEquivalentID/countEquivalentIDs, IntlCalendar::get on a fresh calendar, DateInterval::__set_state) have no stub capabilities, so they are ALL now that 7.x checks builtin calls from pure/read-props contexts (bb1042b9fd). Missing intl stubs, e.g. DateTime.php:234.
addAll(iterable $elements) iterates an unknown iterable (may be a generator), charged impure since dfdcd6de94; psl annotates these external-mutation-free.

entries.message_pattern: /^The context is read-props\|write-this-props\|write-refs but method Psl\\Collection\\MutableSet::remove/
entries.note: offsetUnset() is @psalm-external-mutation-free but calls the unannotated (so impure) remove(); 7.x checks $this calls against declared capabilities (bb1042b9fd).

`throw new MultipleRootNodesException()` in @pure from_list(): the exception ctor calls parent::__construct(), so it is not trivial and, unannotated, is ALL; same for unannotated static factories/methods called from external-mutation-free code. 7.x checks throw new and every call (bb1042b9fd); psl lacks annotations.
@pure function calls a function psl annotates @psalm-mutation-free (= read-props in 7.x), e.g. to_intl_timezone.php -> create_intl_timezone(); a pure context may not read props (bb1042b9fd).
password_hash() draws a random salt, mt_rand() uses the global RNG, random_bytes/random_int read the OS RNG: not pure / external-mutation-free as psl declares (Password\hash @pure, PseudoRandom\int).

entries.message: Calling empty on a boolean value is almost certainly unintended
entries.note: Regression: `empty($x)` on a variable that only some branches define (as a bool) is an isset-style check, but 7.x now keeps the bool type of the possibly-undefined variable and EmptyAnalyzer reports "Calling empty on a boolean value" (e.g. Sql.php:1367 $distinct, ImageStyleDownloadController.php:223 $lock_acquired, DrupalKernel.php:1109 $subrequest). Snippet `if ($c) { $d = true; } if (!empty($d)) {}`: 6.x nothing, 7.x InvalidArgument. Bisected to PR #13751 4d55eb8161 (275e288212 "Keep the type of a variable some branches of an if define, possibly undefined"); EmptyAnalyzer should skip possibly_undefined types.

Regression: the constant is declared once (EntityStorageInterface::FIELD_LOAD_*, MediaSourceInterface::METADATA_*) and reaches the class both through an interface chain and through the parent class; not ambiguous. Snippet (interface Src{const C}, FC extends Src, OI extends FC, abstract Base implements Src, OE extends Base implements OI; OE::C): 6.x nothing, 7.x AmbiguousConstantInheritance. Real contradiction lost; low impact (code depending on missing classes).

`$this->map = new \WeakMap()` into a WeakMap<K, V> property: 7.x infers the open template params of a constructorless new (29417293eb).

entries.message: Cannot access value on variable $_POST using a string offset, expecting int|non-empty-string
entries.note: Read in the true branch of a ternary guarded by isset()/!empty() of the same expression (`isset($x['k']) ? $x['k'] : d`): 6.x did not give the first branch the offset clauses of the condition; 6066bf8add (ternary condition analysed like an if) does (snippet: xmlrpc `isset($filter['number']) ? absint($filter['number'])` reported in 6.x only).

Superglobal ($_POST/$_GET/$_COOKIE/$_SERVER) reported by 6.x as "must be defined prior to use within an unknown function" inside WordPress functions; superglobals are always defined, so the 6.x report was wrong; 7.x superglobal fixes (b4ace24ace, 7919e2a629) are candidates, but a reduced snippet did not reproduce the 6.x report.

$item_id = esc_attr(...) is a string; 6.x widened it to the $_GET item type after `isset($_GET['edit-menu-item']) && $item_id === $_GET[...]` in a ternary (6.x message lists the $_GET value type), 7.x keeps string; a reduced snippet did not reproduce the 6.x widening, so the 7.x change behind it is unknown (6.x was the wrong one).

`global $wpdb;` inside a class method reported by 6.x as InvalidGlobal ("Cannot use global scope here"), which is wrong for a method body; dffdfe4d22 (#9773) changed InvalidGlobal only for files documenting $this; cause of the 6.x report not found, possibly nondeterministic.

`global $wpdb;` inside a class method reported by 6.x as InvalidGlobal ("Cannot use global scope here"), which is wrong for a method body; dffdfe4d22 (#9773) changed InvalidGlobal only for files documenting $this; cause of the 6.x report not found, possibly nondeterministic.

Same function/top-level scope has an UndefinedFunction/UndefinedConstant 7.x newly reports (8e1b0d0158 / 2593074387): 6.x analysed it with function/constant checks off after function_exists()/!defined(), which changes types around unchecked calls; not verified per issue.

Superglobal ($_POST/$_GET/$_COOKIE/$_SERVER) reported by 6.x as "must be defined prior to use within an unknown function" inside WordPress functions; superglobals are always defined, so the 6.x report was wrong; 7.x superglobal fixes (b4ace24ace, 7919e2a629) are candidates, but a reduced snippet did not reproduce the 6.x report.

Superglobal ($_POST/$_GET/$_COOKIE/$_SERVER) reported by 6.x as "must be defined prior to use within an unknown function" inside WordPress functions; superglobals are always defined, so the 6.x report was wrong; 7.x superglobal fixes (b4ace24ace, 7919e2a629) are candidates, but a reduced snippet did not reproduce the 6.x report.

WordPress hash notation (`@return array {` + `@type` lines) is now read as a description (d4dbda1817, PR #12416): 6.x reported InvalidDocblock and dropped the whole docblock (params, return, @global), hence MissingReturnType on the function, and Mixed*/Possibly* in its body and on values its callers got from it (e.g. class-wp-meta-query.php get_sql_clauses() `@return string[] {`).

@global docblock types are now docblock-provided (cfeae2cdc1/78248bf856), so a redundant/impossible check on such a global is reported with the *GivenDocblockType/DocblockTypeContradiction variant instead (pass-1 snippet).
A callable is never falsy; f303c1476a (PR #14322, #13806) stops reporting RiskyTruthyFalsyComparison on callable|null/false (snippet: `?callable $c; if ($c)` reported by 6.x only).
